thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: runtime-worker group us-west2-gpu showing repeated OOMs + CUDA driver resets across 6 nodes. 3 containers crashed in last 8m, autoscaler started replacements. Severity: sev2.
Maya: seeing the same in dashboards — p99 latency spiking, error-rate up ~8%. stack traces include "cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" and "memory allocation failed" logs.
Leon: adding notes — affected jobs are mostly long-context chat requests hitting attention paging. Likely slow KV cache growth + allocator fragmentation.
Ashok: can someone grab `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi` from one of the failed nodes? I want to confirm if it's driver resets or OOM-kill by kernel.
Maya: pasted from node gpu-12 (truncated):
```
[ 12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 41234 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:150000000kB, anon-rss:120000000kB, file-rss:0kB
[ 12345.679012] docker-containerd[3123]: container 41234 exited with code 137
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:06:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
Leon: 79 is GPU HW error/driver fatal -> suggests a hard GPU fault after OOM attempts. But the root cause still looks like memory creep.
Tim: Customer impact — two mid-tier customers reported elevated latencies & a small number of request failures. CS_Liaison is on the calls.
CS_Liaison: confirmed, one customer saw 5% request failures and timeouts; they're asking for ETA. We're prepping a short note.
Ashok: mitigation plan I propose now: 1) reduce attention paging threshold on runtime to force smaller active KV-resident set; 2) enable aggressive KV eviction for affected pools (`--kv-evict-target=0.45 --kv-evict-interval=30s`); 3) temporarily scale up dedicated fallback capacity to route failing requests; 4) restart crashed containers after clearing KV caches.
Maya: on it — I'm patching a quick config change to the runtime pool for us-west2: lower `attn_paging_max_seq_len` and `kv_reserve_ratio`. Will push a canary to 2 nodes first.
Leon: I'll run a live check for fragmentation stats. Run on gpu-12: `curl -s http://localhost:9753/debug/allocator | jq .slab_usage` -> returns allocation histogram showing lots of tiny free slots and many pinned slab fragments. Looks like slab-siphoning pattern.
Ashok: paste the output if you can.
Leon:
```
"slab_usage": {"small_slots_free": 120, "small_slots_inuse": 4520, "pages_fragmented": 1873, "kv_pages": 42300}
"eviction_candidates": 2400
```
Maya: eviction candidates are high and fragmentation ratio > 0.3. That matches slow creep.
InfraBot: Autoscaler already spun up replacement nodes; 2 are healthy, 1 is still flapping (gpu-14). Suggest cordon gpu-14 and drain before further replacements.
Ashok: agreed. Leon, can you evict prefixes for top 10 heavy keys from the offending pool? We have a helper: `redis-kv-tool evict --pool runtime-usw2 --top 10`. That should shave some retained KV pages.
Leon: running it now.
InfraBot: Command executed, evicted 9/10 keys, reclaimed ~22 GB.
Maya: can we also lower batch sizes in the queued worker to reduce transient peak allocations? I can flip `max_tokens_batch=512 -> 256` in the pool config.
Tim: do it. Also enable request throttling for new signups to protect customers.
Maya: changed batch size on canary nodes and enabled throttling rule (`/v1/*` qps down 30%). Canary nodes stable for 5m, no new OOMs.
Leon: fragmentation metrics trending down after forced evictions, p99 latency still elevated but improving.
Ashok: next steps: 1) keep eviction aggressiveness for 2h, 2) schedule a rolling restart of runtime-worker on all affected hosts with `--clear-kv-on-restart`, 3) long-term: increase slab defragmentation sweep frequency and tune page compaction.
CS_Liaison: Customer update ready: "We mitigated a memory growth issue by temporarily reducing batch sizes and forcing cache evictions; performance is improving and we have full engineering attention. We expect normal service within 2 hours."
Maya: initiating rolling restart — issuing `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker -n prod --selector=region=us-west2 --grace-period=120` but will do in 1 node increments.
Leon: watch logs for `KVCache: reclaimed` and no `cuCtxSynchronize` errors. If we see repeat Xid 79, escalate to hardware team for node replace.
Maya: first node restarted cleanly, logs show `KVCache: reclaimed 24.1GB`. No CUDA resets.
Ashok: I'm going to open an infra-ticket to RMA gpu-14 once we confirm it's still flapping after drain. Leon, please collect core dump + nv-state if it flaps again.
InfraBot: Created ticket INF-4482 for gpu-14 RMA.
Tim: thanks team. Maya/Ashok/Leon you'll sign out in ~30m? Who's taking next shift?
Maya: I'm off in 28m. @Leon please take handoff if stable.
Leon: happy to. I'll keep aggressive eviction on and monitor for 1h. If anything recurs, I'll escalate to Ashok and open a full incident page.
CS_Liaison: Customer notified. No SLA breach expected given rapid mitigation, but we keep them updated.
Maya: handoff note: mitigations applied (forced evict, reduced batching, throttles), canary stable, rolling restarts started. Watchlist: gpu-14, fragmentation >0.25, eviction candidates >2000.
Leon: taking handoff. Leaving a short checklist: `1) watch /debug/allocator`, `2) tail runtime logs for Xid 79 or OOM patterns`, `3) check autoscaler churn`, `4) keep CS in loop`.
Ashok: good handoff. I'll draft a follow-up action item: add periodic slab compaction job and a KV growth alert at 15GB/hr.
Leon: noted. If we get clean 1h, I'll mark this thread for closure and add notes to the post-incident doc. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident cleared to monitoring; still on watch.
